affordance_in_statement: The system architecture enforces a strict two-tier design: the microservices can be partitioned into two distinct tiers ... such that every shared volume is accessed by exactly one microservice from the first tier and one from the second tier.
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the same tractable task: the two-tier condition is the bipartite-graph structure enabling the matching-based solution. Removing it would turn the problem into general maximum independent set, changing the computational problem.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the conflict graph as bipartite and uses maximum matching to derive a maximum independent set.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses BFS bipartitioning and the bipartite maximum-independent-set reduction.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The system architecture enforces a strict two-tier design ... every shared volume is accessed by exactly one microservice from the first tier and one from the second tier.

common_affordance: The guaranteed two-tier architecture makes the conflict graph bipartite, allowing maximum independent set to be computed through bipartite matching.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It bipartitions the graph but treats choosing a whole color class, or otherwise comparing color-class sizes, as sufficient; a maximum independent set may combine vertices from both sides and requires a matching-based computation.
Its component/color-class approach similarly assumes that selecting a larger bipartition side gives the optimum, which is false for general bipartite graphs.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat both surviving solutions while preserving the stated computational task. The only decisive edit would be to remove the two-tier/bipartite guarantee and allow arbitrary conflict graphs, but that changes the problem into general maximum independent set.
regression_risk: Removing the bipartite guarantee would also invalidate the defeated students' color-class shortcuts, but it would make the problem computationally intractable under the given bounds.
